answer: Unique-Context Ledger. Each agent identity must reference a distinct physical sensor pigment signature captured at registration, and duplicate patterns are rejected at the vertex of the ingestion graph. Agents must also append a fresh, locally generated event echo within every epoch; replaying another agent's echo fails signature verification. An attacker therefore needs one genuine, physically distinct sensor source and sustained real-world activity per identity, making mass fabrication costly in hardware and operations rather than capital.
